problem_type: A value the model named is neither validated nor observable: the shared admission boundary drops unknown generation parameters silently, and the canvas write path stores an unchecked model identity that the canvas read projection never returns.
symptom: An external MCP host asks Nomi to plan 'Seedance 2.5, 720p, no audio'. Its parameter key is not one this model declares, so the plan succeeds, the spend card shows a normal price, and the delivered clip is 1080p with audio. Nothing reports an error anywhere. The same host can also create a canvas node with a model key the catalog does not have; the node is created, looks normal, and no read tool ever shows which model it carries.
direct_cause: compileParameters pushed unknown keys onto contract.droppedFields and continued; droppedFields had no production reader. bindModelIdentity stored vendor/modelKey verbatim with a comment deferring validation to the UI, and canvasRead's strict node schema declared no model field at all.
class_root: Nomi has no single owner for 'which parameters and which model identity this model accepts'. The knowledge exists in three unreconciled places (curated archetype params in the renderer, the catalog-derived module parameterSchema used by the spend path, and the video archetype projection that overrides it), the external MCP face is told none of them, and the one boundary that could still have caught a wrong value was built to discard it instead of refusing it.

invariant_owner_layer.note: 参数值层这条不变量从此归 compileParameters/compileExecutionContract 这一层管，它有自己的类级测试。画布那半条（模型身份写入校验 + 读回）的 owner 是 canvasNodeFactory 的注入点加 core.assertCatalogModelIdentity，测试是 electron/capabilityCore/nodeModelIdentity.class.test.ts。两半合起来才是这份合同的不变量，主 owner 填参数那一层，因为它是花钱那条路上的最后一道闸。

affected_population: Every external MCP host (Claude Code, Codex) driving generation through nomi_operation_plan / nomi_operation_preview — it has no read tool returning parameter names, so every parameter it sends is a guess.

The in-app Agent for image/audio/3d models: it is told the archetype's params while the spend path validates against the catalog's onboarding-derived schema, so an archetype-declared key absent from onboarding fields was silently discarded.
Every caller of nomi_canvas_edit / add_nodes that names vendor+modelKey: unknown identities were stored and were unreadable afterwards.
entry_points: Single-shot preview and gate_request compile a contract through compileExecutionContract.
Multi-shot draft sealing compiles one sub-contract per included shot through the same function.
MCP canvas writes create nodes through canvasGraph.addNodes, which builds them with the shared canvasNodeFactory.
The MCP canvas read projects nodes through projectCanvasRead.

external_sources.purpose: Decides how a rejected parameter must be reported: 'Input validation errors (e.g., date in wrong format, value out of range)' are Tool Execution Errors, and 'Clients SHOULD provide tool execution errors to language models to enable self-correction.' Also 'Servers MUST: Validate all tool inputs', and the Stateful Tools guidance that an unknown handle 'should return a tool execution error that says so, so the model can recover'. This is why the rejection carries the legal keys, the nearest key and the legal values instead of a generic message.

Prior art for tiered disclosure: a gateway 'replaces the upstream tool list with two meta-tools (get_tool and invoke_tool) so clients see only a lightweight index', and the article states this is a pattern layered on top of MCP rather than a protocol feature. Basis for keeping the rejection message free of a 100-model dump and pointing at the thin list instead.

invariants: A generation parameter the caller named is either accepted into the contract or refused with a structured reason; it is never discarded while the call reports success.
A refusal carries what the caller needs to be right next time: the legal keys (or the nearest key), the legal values, the declared range, or the declared variants.
A key that cannot be proven wrong is not refused, and is not discarded either: it stays in the contract with a warning that says it was not validated.
Parameter keys that are Nomi's own planning intent rather than provider parameters are a named vocabulary, not an accident of the unknown-key path.
Leftover parameters from a previous model are removed where the model changes, and the change is reported, instead of being absorbed by the admission layer.
A model identity written onto a canvas node exists in the catalog and matches the node's media kind, and is readable back through the canvas read projection.

door_reduction.why_not: This change closes the value-layer holes at the doors that already existed; it does not merge any door, so the count is unchanged and every surviving door is justified here. The three compileExecutionContract doors are three lifecycle moments (single-shot preview, single-shot gate_request, multi-shot seal) that must each compile their own contract because each is a separate spend-boundary decision; they already converge on the one compileParameters they all call, which is where the invariant now lives. The two buildCanvasNode doors are the renderer and the Electron/MCP path of the same shared factory — that is the intended single factory with two dependency injections, not two implementations; only the MCP door receives an external model identity, and the renderer door passes an already-assembled meta, so only the MCP door needs the validator. The deriveModelListing / buildAgentModelEntries doors are the two model-catalog projections that this change deliberately did NOT unify (see residual_risks): the renderer-side archetype registry is not reachable from the main process because .dependency-cruiser.mjs rule electron-no-import-src is a hard zero, so unifying them is an architectural move of its own and is out of this change's scope.

generality_proof: Every generation path that can spend money compiles its contract through compileExecutionContract, and every one of them reaches compileParameters — single-shot preview, single-shot gate_request, and multi-shot seal. Putting the refusal in compileParameters therefore covers the whole class rather than the reported example: it does not matter which face (in-app lane or external MCP), which provider, which model kind, or whether the parameter schema came from the catalog module manifest or from the video archetype override, because all of those are already funnelled into the single `module.parameterSchema` this function reads. The same argument holds for the canvas half: both the renderer and the MCP path build nodes through the one canvasNodeFactory, and only the MCP path supplies an external identity, so injecting the validator into that factory covers every caller that can supply an unvalidated identity, while projectCanvasRead is the single projection every canvas read of every face goes through.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: The one admission boundary for generation parameter values. Accepts a declared key whose value matches its declared type, enum and range; refuses anything provably wrong with a ParameterRejection naming the legal keys, the nearest key, the legal values or the range; passes through, with a warning, only what it cannot prove wrong; and treats the named planning-hint vocabulary as neither a parameter nor a mistake.

Refuses a variantId that is not one of the variants the selected model declares, listing the ones it has. Callers that can resolve the variant list must pass it; not passing it means the list is unavailable, never that any value is acceptable.

Binds an externally supplied vendor/modelKey onto a node only after the injected assertModelIdentity accepts it. The factory keeps its zero-import purity, so the catalog-backed judgement is injected rather than imported.

The catalog-backed judgement itself: the named model must exist in listAvailableModels() (the one App-wide answer to 'which models exist and can be used') and its kind must match the node's media kind.

Returns each node's bound model identity so a wrong identity is observable, reading the same meta keys the generation resolver reads, and carrying identity only — parameters stay in the per-model detail tier.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: Calls compileExecutionContract with the video parameter schema and now also with videoAllowedVariantIds; nomiMcpGenerationPlanning.test.ts drives it through the real MCP protocol harness and observes the refusal of an unsupported parameter that this test previously asserted was dropped.
Second compileExecutionContract call site in the same file, wired identically; it is the spend boundary, so it must refuse the same values preview refuses rather than re-deriving its own judgement.
Compiles one sub-contract per included shot through the same function and now receives videoAllowedVariantIds through its deps; the multi-shot entrance e2e test exercises this path.

The renderer never passes spec.vendor/spec.modelKey — it passes an already-assembled input.meta built from the catalog by the UI — so bindModelIdentity's external-identity branch is unreachable from this door and the validator is intentionally not injected there.
Reads only vendor and modelKey off the listing to compute the run-level allowed set; it consumes no parameter or reference-capability knowledge, so the three-source parameter split does not reach it.

recurrence.reason: The mechanism is not tied to one model or one provider. Any parameter key any face sends for any of the 100+ catalog models went through the same discard branch, and the discard was invisible by construction because the ledger recording it had no reader. The same is true of the canvas identity: every MCP caller naming a model reached the same unchecked binding. New providers, new models and new callers all inherit the mechanism until the shared boundary owns the rule.
same_class_scan: node scripts/door-map.mjs compileExecutionContract compileParameters — 3 write doors, 0 read doors; all three compile sites now pass through the hardened function.

node scripts/door-map.mjs bindModelIdentity buildCanvasNode — 3 write doors; the renderer door was inspected and shown not to carry an external identity (canvasNodeActions.ts passes input.meta, never vendor/modelKey).

node scripts/door-map.mjs deriveModelListing listAvailableModels buildAgentModelEntries listAvailableModelsForAgent — 5 write doors and 7 read doors, which is the evidence for the three-source parameter split recorded in class_root and for the residual risk below.

grep -rn droppedFields across electron/ src/ scripts/ tests/ — the only non-test occurrences were the definition and the two push sites, confirming the ledger had no production reader before it was removed.

Running the full electron suite surfaced two further populations that had been riding the same silent-discard path and are now named explicitly: Nomi's own planning hints read by videoRecommendationInput, and models whose catalog row declares no parameter schema at all.

prevention.invariant: A caller-named generation parameter is accepted, or refused with the facts needed to correct it, or explicitly carried through as unvalidated — never discarded behind a successful response. A caller-named model identity on a canvas node exists in the catalog, matches the node kind, and is readable back.
prevention.failure_mode: ContractCompilationError carrying a ParameterRejection (unknown_parameter / parameter_type_mismatch / parameter_not_in_enum / parameter_out_of_range / missing_required_parameter / unknown_variant), and CanvasGraphError('unknown_model_identity') on the canvas write path. Both fail closed before any provider call or any durable write.
prevention.strategy: The rule lives in the one function all three spend paths already funnel through, and in the one node factory both canvas write paths already share, so no caller can opt out and no new caller can be added that bypasses it. The two legitimate non-provider key populations are named vocabularies rather than holes: GENERATION_PLANNING_HINT_KEYS is asserted to equal what the recommendation reader consumes, and an empty declared schema keeps the value plus a warning instead of dropping it. Cross-model leftovers are cleaned where the model changes and reported in the existing changeset, so the admission layer never has to be deaf to make model switching work.

legacy_paths.rationale: The DroppedField type, the droppedFields field on ExecutionContractV1 and both push sites are deleted in the same change; there is no flag, fallback or compatibility branch that can still reach the old discard behaviour. The fixtures that carried droppedFields in test data were updated in the same commit.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: The invariant is owned entirely by Nomi's own admission boundary and catalog. No third-party runtime decides whether a parameter key is legal; the MCP specification informed the shape of the error but is not a dependency version that can drift this behaviour.

migration: No stored data changes shape. Drafts persisted before this change can carry parameters the selected model does not declare; they now surface a structured refusal at preview instead of silently losing the value, and the model-switch path strips such leftovers and reports them in changeset.clearedParameters. Contracts persisted with a droppedFields field are still readable because nothing reads that field; it simply stops being written.
residual_risks: The three-source split named in class_root is reduced but not eliminated. The catalog-derived module parameterSchema and the video archetype projection are now the single admission judgement that both faces are measured against, but the renderer's curated archetype params (src/config/modelArchetypes) remain a separate source for what the in-app Agent is told about image/audio/3d models. Unifying them requires moving 42 archetype data files out of the renderer, which .dependency-cruiser.mjs rule electron-no-import-src (hard zero) makes a prerequisite rather than an option; that is its own change.

Tiered disclosure of the model spec itself (a thin list plus a per-model detail on both faces) is NOT implemented in this change. The external MCP face still returns only ModelListingEntry from nomi_read{target:"models"} and has no target:"model" detail, so it still cannot discover parameter names before sending them — it now gets a refusal naming the legal keys instead of a silent discard, which makes the second attempt correct, but the first attempt is still a guess.

ParameterField.min/max is only populated where the source declares a range: the video archetype controls carry min/max, while catalog onboarding fields do not, so out-of-range values on non-video models remain unjudgeable. This is a gap in the catalog data, not in the boundary; the boundary judges what is declared and passes the rest through with a warning rather than pretending.

assertCatalogModelIdentity reads listAvailableModels(), which reads the catalog from disk on every call. That is the same non-caching discipline usableVideoModelCandidates deliberately adopted, but it means node creation now touches the catalog; no performance measurement was taken for large batch node creation.
The real-model tool-accuracy measurement required by R13.3 was not run in this change, so no before/after write-accuracy or turn-success numbers are recorded for it.

assertCatalogModelIdentity 住在新文件 electron/capabilityCore/canvasModelIdentity.ts（core.ts 贴 800 行门岗，放不下）。它是叶子纯函数，自身不调用任何本文件符号，所以 door-map 生成不出一扇指向它的门；合同的 scope_paths 因此不列它，它由调用方 core.ts 那扇门代表。这是 door-map「只数调用点」的已知盲区，不是漏数。
